note: Full run, 50/50 batches, 496 grammar points (labels, forms, explanations EN+pt-BR). confirmed = 2-vote unanimous. Dominant confirmed class = FALSE FORMATION RULES in explanations (attachment rules that license ungrammatical learner output). Verifiers rejected 30, several because the proposed FIX was harmful: narrowing the copula entry to na-adjectives would have barred the standard 高いです, and one fix would have written pt-BR prose into `caution`, a closed neutral-English enum. Apply needs owner go-ahead.

findings.issue: Wrong formation rule. じゃいけない is restricted to nouns/na-adjectives, but its main use is with verbs whose て-form is voiced (読んじゃいけない, 飲んじゃいけない, 泳いじゃいけない). As written the learner will produce *読んちゃいけない. It also contradicts forms[1] ('após som sonoro').
findings.current: じゃいけない aparece com substantivos e adjetivos-な ('não pode ser hoje').
findings.suggested: じゃいけない vem de verbos cuja forma-て termina em で (読んじゃいけない) e também de substantivos e adjetivos-な ('não pode ser hoje').
findings.fix: ちゃいけない vem de verbos cuja forma-て termina em て (食べちゃいけない, 行っちゃいけない). じゃいけない vem de verbos cuja forma-て termina em で (飲んじゃいけない, 読んじゃいけない) e também de substantivos e adjetivos-な ('não pode ser hoje').
notes: じゃ is the ではは-contraction of any で-ending て-form (飲んじゃ, 読んじゃ, 泳いじゃ); limiting it to nouns/na-adj teaches *飲んちゃ and contradicts forms[1] 'após som sonoro'.
Real: 読んではいけない→読んじゃいけない is high-frequency; text implies all verbs take ちゃ (*読んちゃ) and contradicts forms[1] 'após som sonoro'.

findings.issue: Same wrong formation rule as expl_pt: ちゃ is claimed for all action verbs and じゃ only for nouns/na-adjectives. Verbs whose て-form ends in で take じゃ (読んじゃいけない), so the stated attachment rule teaches a false conjugation.
findings.current: ちゃいけない comes from action verbs (...). じゃいけない appears with nouns and な-adjectives ('it can't be today').
findings.suggested: ちゃいけない comes from 〜ては (食べちゃ); verbs whose て-form ends in で take じゃ (読んじゃいけない), as do nouns and な-adjectives ('it can't be today').
findings.fix: ちゃいけない comes from verbs whose て-form ends in て (食べちゃいけない, 行っちゃいけない). じゃいけない comes from verbs whose て-form ends in で (飲んじゃいけない, 読んじゃいけない) and also from nouns and な-adjectives ('it can't be today').
notes: Same false conjugation rule in en: ちゃ is not the verb-only variant. Fix is right but should mirror the pt wording and use core N5 verbs.
Same false conjugation rule; ぶ/む/ぬ/ぐ verbs voice the て-form and take じゃ (飲んじゃいけない), so 'nouns and な-adjectives' is not just incomplete but misleading.

findings.issue: Says the copula links the subject to 'um substantivo ou adjetivo', with no restriction. だ never follows an い-adjective (*高いだ) — only nouns and な-adjectives. Stated this way it licenses the classic beginner error.
findings.current: a palavrinha que liga o sujeito a um substantivo ou adjetivo, como o nosso 'ser/estar'
findings.suggested: a palavrinha que liga o sujeito a um substantivo ou adjetivo-な, como o nosso 'ser/estar' (だ nunca vem depois de adjetivo-い: 高い, não 高いだ)
findings.fix: No change needed. The proposed fix is actively harmful: restricting the copula to 'substantivo ou adjetivo-な' would make the standard N5 form 高いです look ungrammatical, since this entry covers だ AND です jointly. The *高いだ pitfall belongs in gram:i-adjectives (where it is already handled) or in a note field, not in the copula's definition sentence.
notes: Describes the copula's function, not an attachment rule; だ does follow な-adjectives (きれいだ) and です does follow い-adjectives (高いです), so the suggested restriction would wrongly bar 高いです.
Omission, not error: entry never claims だ follows い-adj (both examples are nouns), 高いです IS valid, and gram:i-adjectives already teaches 'conjuga sem precisar de verbo ser'.

findings.issue: Same unrestricted attachment claim: the copula is said to link the subject to 'a noun or adjective'. だ cannot follow an い-adjective (*高いだ); only nouns and な-adjectives take だ.
findings.current: the little word that links the subject to a noun or adjective, like our 'to be'
findings.suggested: the little word that links the subject to a noun or な-adjective, like our 'to be' (だ never follows an い-adjective: 高い, not 高いだ)
findings.fix: No change needed. The suggested 'noun or な-adjective' wording would falsely bar 高いです, one of the earliest forms an N5 learner produces, because the entry defines だ and です together. If the pitfall is wanted here it must be stated as a だ-specific caveat (e.g. 'だ, ao contrário de です, não vem depois de adjetivo-い'), not by narrowing the copula's definition.
notes: Same as expl_pt: 'noun or adjective' is a defensible functional gloss for an entry covering both だ and です (高いです is standard); both examples are nouns. い-adj pitfall belongs in the い-adjective entry.
Same: 'links the subject to a noun or adjective' is a defensible beginner gloss true of です (高いです); nothing in the entry licenses *高いだ.

findings.issue: ～てはいけません is tagged caution "rough", which conflicts with register ["polite"] and misleads: the form is the standard polite prohibition used on public signs and by teachers, not coarse/vulgar language. The real warning is that it is a strong, top-down prohibition, so it should not be aimed at superiors or customers.
findings.current: rough
findings.suggested: Proibição forte e vertical (de quem tem autoridade); evite usar com superiores ou clientes.
findings.fix: Proibição forte e vertical (de quem tem autoridade); evite usar com superiores ou clientes.
notes: caution is a closed enum (none/rough/offensive/sensitive); rough=blunt/top-down, not vulgar (なさい "gentle command" is also rough). polite+rough is by design; fix puts pt prose in a neutral enum.
caution is a closed enum (none/rough/offensive/sensitive); 'rough' = blunt/top-down, not vulgar (that's 'offensive'); fix would put pt-BR prose in a neutral-English enum.

findings.issue: になる is not restricted to unintentional change — the item's own example 先生になる ('become a teacher') is a deliberate goal, so the stated nuance contradicts it. The real contrast is agentive 〜にする (someone makes X become Y) vs 〜になる (the subject undergoes the change). expl_en carries the identical sentence and needs the same fix so the two stay consistent.
findings.current: O foco está na transformação natural, não em alguém fazendo a mudança de propósito.
findings.suggested: O foco é o sujeito que passa pela mudança; quando alguém transforma algo de propósito, usa-se 〜にする.
findings.fix: O foco é o sujeito que passa pela mudança; quando alguém transforma algo de propósito, usa-se 〜にする.
notes: Mainstream DBJG-style contrast (spontaneous change vs agent-caused 〜にする), hedged as 'o foco'; in 先生になる the subject still undergoes the change, so nothing false for N5.
Standard non-agentive framing (cf. DBJG: naru = change without an agent's direct involvement, vs ni suru). 先生になる has no external agent, so no contradiction. Defensible, not major.

findings.fix: The literal logic is a double negative: 'if I don't do it, it won't do' (i.e., 'it's mandatory to do'). It's very common in everyday speech among friends, family, and relaxed situations. It sounds lighter and more natural in conversation than the long, formal forms.
notes: Unclosed paren is real and expl_pt proves intent; but the proposed span leaves the stray ')' after 'formal forms.' unmatched.

findings.issue: Neither the explanation, the pattern nor the form states what precedes に: the verb must be in the ます-stem (食べに行く), or a verbal noun (買い物に行く). As written, a learner will produce the classic error 食べるに行く. expl_pt has the same gap.
findings.current: The particle に here marks the purpose of the trip.
findings.suggested: Before に the verb takes the ます-stem (食べに行く); a noun of activity also works (買い物に行く). に here marks purpose.
findings.fix: The particle に here marks the purpose of the trip. Before に the verb goes in the ます-stem (the ます form minus ます): 食べに行く "go eat" — never 食べるに行く. A noun that names an activity also works: 買い物に行く "go shopping".
notes: Label/pattern/form/expl never state the attachment; no Japanese example at all (unlike every sibling entry), so 食べるに行く is the predictable output. expl_pt needs the same addition.
Real gap: no field states V-ます-stem+に and the entry has no Japanese example at all, so 食べるに行く is the predictable error; gp-35 in this batch does state its attachment.

findings.issue: label_en's "how come" is rendered as "como", which in pt-BR means "how" (= どうやって). Placed beside "por quê" it teaches that なんで can mean "how/in what way" as a manner question, which is false.
findings.current: por quê / como (なんで)
findings.suggested: por quê / como assim (なんで)
findings.fix: por quê / como assim (なんで)
notes: なんで is 何で; the instrumental 'how/by what means' reading is real and expl_en itself flags it, so 'como' is not false. en-pt label looseness is stylistic, not a defect.
Finding's premise is wrong: pt-BR "como" covers means, and the 何で instrumental reading is real and documented in this entry's own explanation, which ranks "por quê" as the N5 core use.

findings.issue: どこも alone is not the 'nowhere' form with motion verbs: the particle must precede も (どこにも/どこへも行きません). Glossed this way, learners will produce ungrammatical 「どこも行きませんでした」. The gloss should show どこ(に/へ)も.

findings.fix: nowhere (どこ(に/へ)も + negative verb)

Gloss is not false: どこも+neg is grammatical alone in subject slot (どこも開いていません). Particle note belongs in caution/expl, not a meaning gloss.

findings.issue: The advice pattern attaches to the plain PAST (た) form of the verb (行ったほうがいい), with ～ない for negative advice. The pattern field omits た, and expl_en/expl_pt never mention the formation either, so learners will produce 行くほうがいい (a comparison, not advice).

Bare 〜ほうがいい is the standard textbook headword (Genki L14, MnN L32, Bunpro) and also hosts noun+の/adj; forcing た/ない into pattern narrows scope. Gap belongs to expl.

Para dar conselho, o verbo vai na forma passada informal (forma た): 早く寝たほうがいいです = \"é melhor você dormir mais cedo\". Para dizer que é melhor NÃO fazer, use ～ないほうがいい: 今日は行かないほうがいいです." findings.issue: The entry never states the formation rule: 〜まえに requires the verb's dictionary (non-past) form even when the main clause is past, and a noun needs の (授業の前に). As written a learner can produce 食べたまえに or 授業まえに. expl_en has the same gap.

No formation rule stated and, alone in this batch, no Japanese example; V-dict+前に vs N+の+前に is core N5 and 食べた前に is a real learner error. Proposed fix drops the time-quantity case.

findings.issue: The explanation never states what に attaches to. 〜に行く requires the verb's ます-stem (見ます→見に行く) or an action noun (買い物に行く); with only the example 見に行く given, a beginner will produce the wrong form ×映画を見るに行く. The same gap exists in expl_en.

findings.issue: The formation rule for i-adjectives is stated incompletely: い-adjectives do not simply take て, they drop い and take くて. As written it licenses *ひろいて; only the example silently shows the real rule.

findings.fix: adjetivos-i trocam o い final por くて (ひろい → ひろくて); substantivos e adjetivos-na levam で

The `explanation` field is the word-type overview (which connector goes with which class), matching the schema convention used by gram:te-form (explanation = overview, formation = mechanics). The batch file just omits those fields.
As stated the rule is false (licenses *ひろいて); the forms array carries no conjugation info, so expl is the only place the い→くて change can appear.

findings.fix: i-adjectives drop い and take くて (ひろい → ひろくて); nouns and na-adjectives take で

findings.issue: よ is tagged casual-only. It is a spoken/conversational particle that attaches freely to polite ます/です forms (行きますよ, そうですよ), so a 'casual' register class can mislead learners into thinking it is incompatible with polite speech. 'colloquial' alone is accurate.

findings.fix: ["colloquial"] (よ also occurs with polite ます/です forms; it is spoken register, not casual-only)
notes: In this registry 'casual' marks polite-incompatible forms (じゃない, かな, って); よ is core with です/ます (そうですよ). Sibling gram:ne is ['plain','colloquial'] — よ is inconsistent.
よ attaches freely to ます/です (行きますよ, 大丈夫ですよ); in this enum 'casual' contrasts with 'polite', so the tag asserts a false restriction.

findings.issue: たくさん is listed as another way to intensify alongside とても/けっこう, but たくさん is a quantity adverb (modifies verbs/quantities) and cannot intensify an adjective (*たくさん高い). For Brazilians this is exactly the 'muito' trap, so the grouping is misleading. Same wording in expl_en.
findings.current: É a primeira forma de intensificar que o aluno aprende, ao lado de けっこう (razoavelmente) e たくさん (em grande quantidade).
findings.suggested: É a primeira forma de intensificar que o aluno aprende, ao lado de けっこう (bem/bastante); たくさん (muito, em quantidade) modifica verbos, não adjetivos.
findings.fix: expl_pt: "É a primeira forma de intensificar que o aluno aprende, junto com けっこう (bem, bastante). Cuidado: たくさん (muito, em quantidade) acompanha verbos e substantivos, nunca adjetivos." | expl_en (same change): "It is the first intensifier the student learns, together with けっこう (quite, pretty). Note that たくさん (a lot, in quantity) goes with verbs and nouns, never with adjectives."
notes: The gloss '(em grande quantidade)' already separates quantity from degree; the clause is a sequencing remark, not a claim that たくさん高い is legal. Nothing false — stylistic polish only.
Category error: たくさん is a quantity adverb, cannot modify adjectives (*たくさん高い), yet is grouped as an intensifier. Fix expl_en identically.

The en side ("to burst into tears") is fine.

findings.suggested: 泣き出す = "cair no choro / começar a chorar de repente"

"desatar a + inf." is an inceptive periphrasis used in pt-PT; pt-BR uses "cair no choro". Violates the hard pt-BR-only rule and is opaque to a BR beginner. Rest of the gloss list is fine.

findings.issue: Register class is misleading: ではないか is the uncontracted form, typical of written/argumentative style and of stiff, forceful (often masculine, older-sounding) speech. The everyday casual spoken equivalent is the contraction じゃないか, so tagging ではないか as casual/colloquial invites learners to use it in informal conversation.

findings.issue: The parenthesized "(não)" makes the pt label read as "could you NOT do it?", i.e. a request to refrain — the opposite of what the pattern does. findings.issue: Two incompatible analyses are mixed: ように is given a purpose/softening function ("para que"), which fits a purpose clause + pedido, but the label and the example "passe a entender" are the change-of-state 〜ようになってほしい. The explanation never says ように must be followed by なる (or する), so the learner gets no usable formation rule.
findings.current: O ように dá a ideia de "de modo que / para que" e deixa o pedido mais indireto (...) "quero que você passe a entender"
findings.suggested: Aqui o ように vem antes de なる/する: 〜ようになってほしい = "quero que passe a..."; 〜ようにしてほしい = "quero que faça o possível para..."
findings.fix: Estrutura para dizer que você quer que alguém mude de comportamento ou passe a fazer algo. Aqui o ように não aparece sozinho: ele vem antes de なる ou する. 〜ようになってほしい = "quero que (alguém) passe a..." — mudança de estado: 分かるようになってほしい ("quero que você passe a entender"). 〜ようにしてほしい = "quero que (alguém) procure / faça o possível para..." — esforço: 遅れないようにしてほしい ("quero que você evite se atrasar"). O tom é de pedido indireto, mais suave que 〜てください.
notes: ように+Vてほしい genuinely means 'de modo que/para que' (聞こえるように話してほしい); 'verbos de mudança ou esforço' already points at なる/する. Fix over-restricts.
label_pt ("passe a fazer"), pattern ように～てほしい and forms all target ようになる/ようにする, yet expl_pt glosses ように as purpose "para que" and never states なる/する is required.

findings.issue: Wrong formation/class mapping: the godan potential is -eru (話す→話せる, 書く→書ける), never れる. れる attached to a godan verb yields the PASSIVE (書かれる); れる is in fact the colloquial ra-nuki ICHIDAN potential (食べれる). Labeling れる as the godan potential suffix teaches a false rule.

notes: Godan potential is -eru (話せる/書ける); れる on a godan verb gives the passive (書かれる). Label contradicts the entry's own 話せる example.
godan potential is -eru (話す→話せる); れる on a godan gives the PASSIVE 書かれる. Fix must also change form "れる"→"える", else form/gloss contradict.

findings.issue: Mesmo erro do en: o potencial de verbos godan é -eru (話す→話せる), não れる. Com godan, れる produz a voz passiva (書かれる); れる é o potencial coloquial (ra-nuki) dos ichidan (食べれる).

Mesmo defeito: rótulo copiou a tabela da voz passiva (godan れる / ichidan られる). O campo form "れる" também deve virar "える".

findings.issue: 〜ばよかった (affirmative) expresses regret for NOT having done something. Saying the speaker laments an action they 'fez ou deixou de fazer' invites the false inference that 食べればよかった can mean 'I shouldn't have eaten'; regret for an action actually performed requires 〜なければよかった.

findings.issue: Conflates two different が. The contrast example 日本語は話せますが、中国語は話せません has no subject が — the が there is the conjunction "mas". The text calls が the subject particle and illustrates with the unrelated double-subject 象は鼻が長い, so the learner will misparse ...ますが as a subject marker.

findings.fix: É o padrão de CONTRASTE: você fala de dois elementos e opõe um ao outro. A estrutura é "[X]は … が、[Y]は …", em que cada は destaca (tematiza) um dos elementos e o が liga as duas partes com o sentido de "mas" — não é o が de sujeito. Ex.: 日本語は話せますが、中国語は話せません (にほんごははなせますが、ちゅうごくごははなせません) = "Japonês eu falo, chinês não"; コーヒーは飲みますが、お茶は飲みません = "café eu bebo, chá não". Esse は de contraste pode ocupar o lugar do を ou do が do elemento destacado. Cuidado para não confundir com o が de subsujeito de 象は鼻が長い (ぞうははながながい) = "o elefante tem a tromba comprida", que é outra estrutura.
notes: が on a finite predicate (話せます／飲みます) is the conjunction "mas", not subject が; the fix must replace the whole field, not just the clause.

findings.issue: Same conflation in en: the pattern は〜が…は uses が as the conjunction 'but' (as in the given 話せますが example), not the subject particle. Mixing it with the double-subject 象は鼻が長い teaches a false analysis of the pattern's が.

findings.fix: This is the CONTRAST pattern: you mention two elements and set one against the other. The structure is "[X]は … が、[Y]は …", where each は highlights (topicalizes) one element and が joins the two halves with the meaning "but" — it is not the subject が. E.g.: 日本語は話せますが、中国語は話せません (にほんごははなせますが、ちゅうごくごははなせません) = "Japanese I can speak, Chinese I can't"; コーヒーは飲みますが、お茶は飲みません = "coffee I drink, tea I don't." This contrastive は can take the place of the を or the が of the element being highlighted. Careful not to confuse this が with the sub-subject が of 象は鼻が長い (ぞうははながながい) = "the elephant has a long trunk," which is a different structure.
notes: Source pattern は〜が… は puts が right before the second は = conjunctive が; the double-subject reading misparses both examples given.

findings.issue: Conflates というのだ with the explanatory のだ/んです. というのだ is quotative: it reports what someone says/claims ('or so he says'), it does not itself answer a 'why'. Giving a reason requires というのは…からだ. As written, a learner would produce 疲れたというのだ for 'the thing is, I'm tired'.
findings.current: It usually closes the sentence with だ/です (というのだ/というのです) and typically appears in answer to a 'why'.
findings.suggested: As というのだ/というのです it reports what someone claims; to state a reason, use というのは…からだ.
findings.fix: It usually closes the sentence with だ/です (というのだ/というのです), where it reports what someone else says or claims — often as the explanation behind a puzzling situation. To give your own reason directly, use のだ/んです, or というのは…からだ.
notes: Entry omits the quotative core and would license 疲れたというのだ; but the fix over-corrects and drops the useful だ/です note.
Entry omits that という is quotative; as written it models first-person 疲れたというのだ, which is wrong. But it CAN explain a preceding fact, so soften the fix.

findings.issue: "have (someone) do" reads as causative English (〜させる / 〜てもらう) and implies the action was brought about; 〜ように言う only reports the instruction. The pt version does not carry this gloss, so en/pt also diverge.

English "have someone do" also covers delegated instruction ("have him call me back" = 電話するように言ってください), so it is not solely causative; en is the source field, pt need not mirror it word-for-word.
